unmapped_findings: The phase evolution sequence during aging of the Fe-Mn-Al-Cu low-density steels (including 15Al) followed: α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase (b0068).
The elastic modulus of the 15Al alloy, measured through compressive stress-strain curves, is 164 GPa; this value was used in the indentation fracture-toughness equation (b0023).

The study's ultra-wide adjustable hardness range of 253.4–965.6 HV was achieved via aging treatments; for the 15Al alloy the optimal aging temperature range for ultra-high hardness was about 525 °C–600 °C (b0038, b0077).
For the 15Al alloy, at temperatures of 575 °C and above the aging hardening response was significantly accelerated, with a substantial hardness increase after just 1 h of aging (b0037).
